stories.headline: ₹50-crore bio-economy mission proposed for Kalyana Karnataka
stories.deck: The three-year initiative to focus on biotechnology, sustainable agriculture, and rural entrepreneurship across seven districts
stories.bodyText:
The Karnataka government is planning to launch ‘Kalaburagi Bio-Economy Mission 2026’, a three-year initiative with an estimated investment of ₹50 crore, to harness the region’s indigenous biological resources, improve agricultural productivity, increase farmers’ income, and create new employment and entrepreneurial opportunities in rural areas.
Minister for Home, IT, Biotechnology and e-Governance Priyank Kharge, who is in charge of the district, said the proposed mission, conceptualised by the Bengaluru Bioinnovation Centre (BBC), would cover all seven districts of Kalyana Karnataka – Kalaburagi, Bidar, Yadgir, Raichur, Koppal, Ballari, and Vijayanagara. Kalaburagi is proposed to be developed as the principal centre for the initiative.
The mission aims to identify the region’s diverse plant resources, indigenous crops, microorganisms, and other agriculture-related biological resources, and use modern biotechnology to develop agricultural solutions, value-added products, and local manufacturing enterprises.
The proposed mission will focus on six major areas:
- biological crop protection
- value addition to tur dal
- conservation of the Kamalapur red banana variety
- research on indigenous microorganisms
- establishment of an integrated bio-economy industrial park
- promotion of rural entrepreneurship
Under biological crop protection, the programme proposes to develop bio-based solutions to control wilt disease in tur, anthracnose disease in chilli, and thrips infestation. The initiative is intended to reduce dependence on chemical inputs while improving crop health and productivity.
A major component will be the value addition of tur, one of the region’s important agricultural products. Instead of selling it only as a raw commodity, the mission proposes to promote its conversion into protein bars, protein concentrate, high-protein flour, nutritional beverages, and ready-to-eat food products. This is expected to provide a boost to local food-processing industries.
The mission proposes to conserve the indigenous Kamalapur red banana variety of Kalaburagi district through tissue culture technology. It aims to develop the capacity to produce two to three lakh quality saplings every month, thereby encouraging wider cultivation of the distinctive variety.
Another focus area is the identification and preservation of indigenous microorganisms through a proposed regional microbial biobank. Research will be undertaken on microorganisms that can be used in biofertilisers, biological pest control and improvement of soil health.
An integrated bio-economy industrial park is proposed to be established in Kalaburagi. It is envisaged as a hub for research, biomanufacturing, tissue culture, food processing, quality testing, and incubation facilities to support start-ups.
The rural entrepreneurship component will provide training and guidance to farmer producer organisations (FPOs), start-ups and rural entrepreneurs. Assistance will also be extended in product value addition, market linkages and export readiness to encourage the establishment of new enterprises.
During the proposed three-year period, the mission aims to identify the potential of more than 40 local biological products and collect and study between 7,000 and 10,000 soil samples. It also seeks to promote the conservation of indigenous crops, improve agricultural productivity and encourage local manufacturing units based on value-added agricultural products.
Mr. Kharge said the initiative, guided by the vision of ‘From Native Biodiversity to Farmer Prosperity’, could give a new direction to agriculture, industry and the rural economy of Kalyana Karnataka. If implemented, it is expected to improve soil health and crop protection, increase the market value of local agricultural produce, create new business opportunities, and strengthen rural employment.
The Kalaburagi Bio-Economy Mission 2026 is currently at the proposal stage. Its implementation will be subject to preparation of a detailed project report (DPR), a feasibility study, and approval by the State Government, Mr. Kharge said.

stories.headline: Illegal oocyte collection racket: 27 ART centres inspected across Telangana, notices issued to seven hospitals
stories.deck: The investigation also includes examining the involvement of women identified in connection with the case, doctors, IVF centres and intermediaries allegedly facilitating the activities
stories.bodyText:
The Telangana Health Department has intensified its investigation into the alleged illegal oocyte (egg) collection racket, with inspections conducted at 27 of the 44 identified Assisted Reproductive Technology (ART) facilities across the State. Officials have detected 13 regulatory violations in seven hospitals and issued show-cause notices to their managements.
Health Minister C. Damodar Rajanarasimha has directed the department to conduct a comprehensive investigation into alleged illegal activities being carried out under the guise of oocyte collection and initiate stringent action against institutions and individuals found violating prescribed regulations.
Acting on the Minister’s directions, task force teams have been inspecting IVF centres across the State for the past four days. Inspections at the remaining facilities are continuing.
Aspects of investigation
The department said further action would be initiated after a detailed examination of records seized by the police and information obtained from the National ART and Surrogacy Registry. The investigation also includes examining the involvement of women identified in connection with the case, doctors, IVF centres and intermediaries allegedly facilitating the activities.
As part of the investigation, the Health department officials visited the National ART and Surrogacy Registry in New Delhi on November 6 and sought details of the data submitted by registered ART clinics and ART banks operating in Telangana.
The department has reiterated that oocyte collection must strictly comply with the provisions of the Assisted Reproductive Technology (Regulation) Act and Rules. All ART clinics and ART banks operating in the State are required to obtain mandatory statutory registration and adhere to the prescribed regulatory framework.
The Health Department also cautioned women against falling prey to misleading assurances and financial inducements offered by intermediaries, warning that such arrangements could expose them to unauthorised medical procedures.

briefs.headline: Keralam to launch Family Sustainability Mapping to identify children in high-risk environments
briefs.deck: Minister for Women and Child Development Bindhu Krishna says circumstances of families and children will be assessed with cooperation of schools, Anganwadis, local self-government institutions, District Child Protection Units, healthcare workers and police
briefs.bodyText:
The Keralam government will take steps to implement ‘Family Sustainability Mapping’ across the State to identify, at an early stage, children living in high-risk environments, Minister for Women and Child Development Bindhu Krishna has said.
Speaking at a press conference to announce the Ujjwala Balyam Awards on Wednesday (November 11, 2026), she said a decision regarding the mapping was reached during a meeting convened following the death of a two-year-old child in Alappuzha recently due to suspected malnutrition.
The circumstances of families and children will be assessed with the cooperation of schools, Anganwadis, local self-government institutions, District Child Protection Units, healthcare workers and the police. Children facing risks such as malnutrition, neglect, domestic abuse, child labour, begging, school dropouts, substance abuse-related issues or various forms of exploitation will be identified and necessary protection and rehabilitation will be ensured.
“Child protection efforts should not be limited to intervening only after abuse or exploitation has already occurred. The government’s objective is to proactively identify high risk situations and ensure timely protection for children. Coordinated action among various departments and institutions will be strengthened to prevent issues such as sexual abuse, physical and mental abuse, neglect, child labour, child begging, human trafficking and online exploitation,” she said.
Activities will be jointly coordinated by departments including the Department of Women and Child Development, the Health Department, the Police, and the Local Self Government Department. This will enable the strengthening of existing child protection systems as well as the proactive identification of risks and the implementation of preventive measures. The Minister stated that the active participation of society is essential to ensure a safe childhood and equal opportunities for every child and to create an environment in which they can grow up with self confidence.
Ms .Krishna said that a total of 52 children from 14 districts have been chosen for the Ujjwala Balyam Awards for showcasing exemplary talent in arts, sports, literature, science, social work, environmental protection, information technology, agriculture, waste management, humanitarian activities, crafts, sculpture and acts involving extraordinary courage.
The winners were selected by a committee chaired by the District Collector in each district. The award consists of a cash prize of ₹25,000, a citation and a plaque. The awards will be presented at the State-level Children’s Day celebration to be held in Thiruvananthapuram on November 14.
The award recipients are children who have demonstrated excellence in various fields, including social work, environmental protection, information technology, agriculture, waste management, humanitarian activities, crafts, sculpture, and acts involving extraordinary courage.

briefs.headline: Bodies of 2 missing Special Police Officers found in Jammu and Kashmir's Kishtwar; shot multiple times
Two missing policemen found dead in J&K’s Kishtwar
briefs.deck: The deaths of two missing SPOs came a day after terrorists opened fire on CRPF in south Kashmir’s Kulgam and left three personnel injured
briefs.bodyText:
Two Special Police Officers (SPOs) of the J&K Police, who were part of an anti-terror operation, were found dead with bullet wounds, a day after they went missing from a dense forest area in the upper reaches of the Chenab Valley, officials said on Thursday (November 12, 2026).
Official sources said the bodies were spotted after a massive search was launched in the Kiyar Sector of Kishtwar’s Dachhan on Wednesday (November 11, 2026). The victims were identified as SPO Rashpal Kumar, 45, and SPO Bobby Chand, 57, both residents of Kiyar Dachhan, Kishtwar.
Initial reports suggested the duo went missing after accompanying a team from the Army’s 17 Rashtriya Rifles up to the Basnan area in the upper reaches of Kishtwar, with dense forests. The SPOs were part of the Temporary Operating Bases (TOBs), set up by the J&K Police after increased terrorist activity in the upper reaches of Jammu and Kashmir since 2020. Both, however, failed to report back to the TOB Camp Dharna, Sector Marwah, Kishtwar on Wednesday (November 11, 2026).
Official sources said the area resonated with firing after the duo went missing. The mobile phones of the missing policemen also went off after a particular time.
However, the police have not issued any formal statement on the incident. They have not confirmed the involvement of terrorists in it.
The deaths of two missing SPOs came a day after terrorists opened fire on CRPF in south Kashmir’s Kulgam and left three personnel injured.

MLA, farmers protest Centre’s ‘failure to release drought relief’ in Karnataka
briefs.deck: MLA demands release of ₹22,400.58 crore in assistance for 226 drought-hit taluks in Karnataka
briefs.bodyText:
Aland MLA B.R. Patil staged a dharna at the Mahatma Gandhi statue in Kalaburagi city on November 11, accusing the Central Government of neglecting Karnataka’s farmers and failing to respond to the State’s repeated appeals for drought relief.
Mr Patil said the State was facing one of its worst droughts in recent history, with 226 taluks declared drought-hit following a severe deficit in southwest monsoon rainfall in 2026. Crop loss had been reported across 57.93 lakh hectares, including 53.92 lakh hectares of crops and 4.01 lakh hectares of horticultural crops, pushing lakhs of farming families into financial distress.
He said the government of Karnataka had sought ₹20,585.73 crore in assistance under the National Disaster Response Fund (NDRF). Following the revision of relief norms by the Union Government, the State had revised its demand to ₹22,400.58 crore.
Despite repeated representations to the Prime Minister, Union Home Minister and Union Agriculture Minister, the Centre had neither granted an appointment to the State’s representatives nor responded adequately to its appeals, he alleged.
Mr. Patil demanded immediate approval and release of the revised drought relief package. He also sought a loan waiver for distressed farmers, adequate compensation for crop loss, and the use of the FRUITS database (Farmer Registration and Unified Beneficiary Information System) to identify eligible beneficiaries instead of relying on outdated agricultural census data.
The legislator demanded the establishment of fodder banks in every gram panchayat, with adequate funds to ensure the supply of fodder and drinking water for livestock, along with the appointment of nodal officers to monitor relief measures.
Describing the Centre’s response as discriminatory towards Karnataka, he said a national disaster such as drought required coordinated action under the federal system. He urged the BJP-led Union Government to treat the situation as an emergency and extend immediate assistance to protect the livelihood of farmers and revive agricultural activity.
Farmers leaders and activists, including Sharanabasappa Mamshetty, M.B Sajjan, Dharmraj Sahu, Umapati Patil, Kedarlingayya Hiremath, and R. G. Shetgar, and farmers from various taluks were present.

briefs.headline: Protesters clash with police in Spain after huge housing cost rallies
briefs.deck: The size of the demonstrations has been seen as an indicator of public discontent before a snap election set for this month, in which the right-wing opposition is expected to defeat Socialist Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez
briefs.bodyText:
Police fired tear gas as sporadic clashes broke out in Madrid and Barcelona on Wednesday (November 11, 2026) after huge protests across Spain over housing affordability and purchasing power just weeks before an early general election.
Hundreds of thousands of protesters turned out during Spain's first nationwide 24-hour strike since 2012, with authorities estimating around 120,000 demonstrators marched through the capital and more than 50,000 rallied in Barcelona.
Clashes broke out after the protests in Spain's two largest cities, as groups of hooded and masked demonstrators hurled projectiles at police and sparked fires, according to AFP journalists.
Video footage showed large rubbish skips as well as bicycles and pot plants engulfed in flames on roads in Barcelona with heavy contingents of police vans racing through the streets.
Police used rubber bullet launchers and tear gas to disperse small groups of protesters and arrested 18 people in Barcelona.
The size of the demonstrations has been seen as an indicator of public discontent before a snap election set for this month, in which the right-wing opposition is expected to defeat Socialist Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez.
Braving pouring rain, protesters in Madrid carried placards shaped like houses and chanted "we have no home" as they called for more affordable housing.
"People work a lot and it isn't enough to pay the rent, to pay for a house," Paula Diaz, a 25-year-old theatre technician who lives with her parents, told AFP at the Madrid protest.
"I hope a government that benefits us comes to power, especially the working class," she added, referring to the November 29 election.
In Barcelona, where authorities estimated 55,000 people marched through the city's luxury Passeig de Gracia commercial thoroughfare, Maria Pinana told AFP "the law of supply and demand does not apply to housing".
"The price of rents should be regulated," said the 34-year-old microbiologist, who lives with friends in a flat where parts of the ceiling have collapsed.
Tens of thousands more attended rallies held in other cities across Spain, the latest in a wave of protests sparked by the eviction of an 87-year-old Madrid pensioner in September.
‘Failure’
In Madrid, where many shops opened as normal, demonstrators earlier on Wednesday (November 11) blocked some roads, picket action that was replicated across the country.
Public transport suffered disruptions even with the implementation of minimum service requirements for commuter trains, metros and buses in and around Barcelona.
In contrast, Madrid's metro said 93% of its trains ran in the early morning, although passenger numbers were down by around half.
UGT union leader Pepe Alvarez told public broadcaster RTVE that the participation was "massive", with a "total" stoppage in some regions making the strike "a huge success".
But his union acknowledged participation was "uneven", with large mobilisation in the car manufacturing, petrochemicals and meat sectors and in coastal regions.
The CEOE organisation, which represents business leaders, called the strike "a failure", adding in a statement that activity had gone ahead normally in most sectors.
Electricity demand had fallen by around five percent, "significantly lower" than in previous strikes, the CEOE said.
‘New cycle’
The main UGT and CCOO unions called the strike following a wave of nationwide protests over access to housing.
Valeria Racu, spokeswoman for the Madrid Tenants' Union which has been at the forefront of protests for weeks, vowed to "put an end to the housing business in this country".
"A new cycle is beginning with trade unionism and conflict at its centre. This day of strikes has been a resounding success," she said.
Mr. Sanchez called this month's election, initially scheduled for 2027, after his minority government failed to secure parliamentary approval for a package of housing measures proposed in response to the demonstrations.
Business groups and the right have rejected the strike, seeing it as an election-related gambit rather than a genuine labour dispute.
But unions have defended the walkout as an exceptional measure intended to generate broad social pressure for action on soaring housing costs.
Isabel Iglesias, a nurse who lives in Madrid, said housing was the issue "that is affecting me the most". She pays 1,000 euros ($1,100) in rent with her partner but earns just 1,700 euros a month.
Ms. Iglesias, 27, said Mr. Sanchez, who has been in power since 2018, "could have done much more" on housing, urging the next government "to listen to everyone and get their act together".

stories.headline: 'Feel like I’ve won Olympic gold again': MM Somaya as Bengaluru cops recover his stolen medals
stories.deck: In a remarkable turn of events, Bengaluru police apprehended two suspects tied to the burglary of hockey icon MM Somaya's residence, successfully retrieving all eight stolen medals, prominently featuring his 1980 Olympic gold. The suspects, known for their previous crimes, sold two of the medals to a jeweller who allegedly recognized their stolen nature.
stories.bodyText:
BENGALURU: City police Monday arrested two persons in connection with the Oct 28 burglary at hockey legend MM Somaya’s Bengaluru home and recovered his stolen medals, including the 1980 Moscow Olympic gold.
All eight missing medals have been found, said police commissioner Seemant Kumar Singh. Police Tuesday presented Manikya aka Manikanta, 31, a resident of Laggere, and Bharat, 25, from Hosakerehalli in Banashankari 3rd Stage, in court.
They were remanded in police custody for eight days. Both have criminal antecedents.
Hockey legend MM Somaya
The duo told cops they had sold a gold and a silver medal to a jewellery store in Rajajinagar. A police officer said the jeweller bought the medals despite knowing those were stolen. “We will take action against him, too,” he added. Meanwhile, efforts are under way to trace a third accused.
Police recovered a camera, a Kodagu-style sword and an Olympic bag, and seized the two-wheeler used in the crime.
Police verified footage from at least 1,000 CCTV cameras, covering around 80sqkm, to zero in on the suspects.
Manikya and Bharat were picked up near Hagalahalli Cross in Ramanagara. During interrogation, they confessed to the crime and revealed the involvement of one other accomplice.
They revealed that the remaining items, besides gold and silver medals, were kept at the Hoskote home of the third accused. Police conducted searches at the Hoskote house Tuesday and recovered the stolen items.
“I am extremely grateful to Bengaluru police,” Somaya said.
According to the complaint, Somaya, a resident of Binnamangala Manavarthe Kaval (BM Kaval) in New Thippasandra, Bengaluru, had left for his hometown in Kodagu district with his family on Oct 25, 2026.
On Oct 28, Somaya’s neighbours found the main door of his home ajar. They later informed Somaya about a likely break-in.
On rushing back home, Somaya was shocked to find that his house had been broken into, and several valuables, including his medals, missing.

stories.headline: From 50% to 16%: Karnataka flags Centre’s shrinking Metro funding share
stories.deck: The Karnataka government has raised concerns about the disproportionate funding of the Namma Metro project, revealing that the state's contribution now stands at 84% of the total costs, while the Centre's share has sharply decreased. With Bengaluru being a major revenue generator, there's a call for the Centre to reinvest more funds into the city's development.
stories.bodyText:
BENGALURU: From 50:50, it’s down to 84:16. 
Karnataka
 Wednesday claimed the Centre’s contribution to 
Namma Metro
’s capital investment has progressively declined over years, creating a huge imbalance in capital infusion.
“Karnataka is shouldering nearly 84% of the total estimated project cost. Bengaluru is among the highest income-tax-paying and GST-generating cities in India and is a major contributor to foreign exchange earnings. The Centre should reinvest a greater share of the revenue generated from Bengaluru in the city’s infrastructure,” Bengaluru development minister Krishna Byre Gowda said, opening a new flank in the Centre-state faceoff.
Presenting the funding commitments across Metro Phases I, II, IIA, IIB and the estimated cost of Phase III, Gowda said the combined investment stood at Rs 77,891 crore.
Karnataka’s contribution was estimated at Rs 65,291 crore against the Centre’s Rs 12,600 crore, translating into a ratio of nearly 5:1. Or, Karnataka, Gowda argued, was effectively investing nearly Rs 5 for Re 1 contributed by the Centre.

stories.headline: Bengaluru taxi unions oppose Vietnamese private electric taxi aggregator’s entry into Karnataka
stories.deck: Vietnamese conglomerate Vingroup’s electric cab service, Green SM, has secured approval from the Karnataka Transport Department to launch app-based taxi operations across the State
stories.bodyText:
Vietnamese conglomerate Vingroup’s electric cab service, Green SM, has secured approval from the Karnataka Transport Department to launch app-based taxi operations across the State, prompting opposition from city-based taxi associations.
A Transport Department official confirmed that the company had been granted permission under the Karnataka On-Demand Transportation Technology Aggregators Rules, 2016. The approval is valid until September 2031.
Organisations, including the Karnataka Rajya Chalakara Parishath and Peace Auto Union, protested against the move on Wednesday, arguing that the entry of another major aggregator could intensify competition and affect drivers’ incomes amid rising operating costs. They have urged the government to reconsider and withdraw the permission.
K. Somashekar, president of the Karnataka Rajya Chalakara Parishath, questioned whether the vehicles had undergone the mandatory inspections. “All cabs must be equipped with fare meters, display boards and prescribed GPS devices,” he said, adding that any licence issued without complying with the regulations should be withdrawn.

stories.headline: Festival of lights turns grim for many as firecracker injuries surge across Bengaluru hospitals
stories.deck: Two burn victims, including a seven-month-old pregnant woman and an eight-year-old boy, are critical; they are being treated in the ICU of the Mahabodhi Burns Centre at Victoria Hospital
stories.bodyText:
The festival of lights turned grim for several people in Bengaluru, with over 200 suffering firecracker-related injuries during Deepavali, including many facing the risk of partial or severe vision loss.
Children, including toddlers as young as two and three years old, and elderly people aged up to 70 were among those affected. A significant proportion of the victims were bystanders who were not even bursting crackers.
Two suffer critical burns
The dangers were not limited to eye injuries. At the Mahabodhi Burns Centre in the State-run Victoria Hospital, seven patients were admitted with significant firecracker-related burn injuries.
Two of them, a 27-year-old pregnant woman who suffered 33% deep burns, including a blast injury to her leg, and an eight-year-old boy who sustained 20% deep burns after a petrol-filled bottle caught fire and was thrown during a firecracker-related incident, are critical. Both are undergoing treatment in the Intensive Care Unit (ICU), while the remaining five patients are stable and receiving treatment in the High Dependency Unit (HDU).
Six other patients with minor firecracker burns were treated as outpatients, said C.N. Yogishwarappa, Professor and Head, Department of Plastic Surgery, at the hospital.
Surge in eye injuries
Hospitals across the city have reported a surge in eye injuries. Narayana Nethralaya treated 114 patients across its Bengaluru centres, while the State-run Minto Ophthalmic Hospital reported 50 cases between November 6 and 11. Sankara Eye Hospital recorded 33 patient entries, Nethradhama treated 12, Prabha Eye Clinic reported 15, and Dr. M.C. Modi Charitable Eye Hospital recorded five cases.
At Minto Ophthalmic Hospital, 30 of the 50 patients suffered grievous injuries and were at risk of partial vision loss, while 20 sustained simple injuries, according to hospital director Dr. Suresh Babu.
Bystanders hit the most
Bystanders accounted for 30 cases, while children made up 20 of the injured. Eleven patients were admitted, three underwent surgery, and the remaining patients were treated as outpatients.
Dr. Babu said the number of cases could exceed the 56 reported last year as more patients were expected to approach the hospital. He suggested that shops selling firecrackers provide protective glasses free of cost to buyers.
At Narayana Nethralaya, 64 patients were treated at the Rajajinagar branch between November 7 and 10, including 33 children and 23 bystanders. Three patients required surgery, while 61 received medical treatment. Across its other centres at Bommasandra, Bannerghatta Road and Whitefield, a subsequent hospital update reported another 56 patients, including 30 children and 12 bystanders. Three patients suffered severe corneal tears requiring surgery. Two toddlers, aged two and three, sustained injuries after soot particles entered their eyes. The oldest patient, aged 70, suffered a conjunctival laceration.
Rohit Shetty, Director, Narayana Nethralaya Eye Hospitals, said the number of children and innocent bystanders among the injured was particularly concerning. He cautioned that seemingly minor injuries could result in prolonged treatment, permanent visual impairment, and lasting trauma.
Cases in other hospitals
Sankara Eye Hospital recorded 33 patient entries, predominantly involving firecracker-related eye injuries. The hospital cautioned against rubbing the eyes or using home remedies and stressed the need for immediate consultation with an ophthalmologist.
Nethradhama treated 12 patients, including six minors, with a five-year-old girl being the youngest. Eight cases were reported on November 10 alone.
The injuries reported across hospitals ranged from eyelid burns, corneal abrasions and foreign particles lodged in the eyes to hyphema, corneal tears and retinal damage.

briefs.headline: Goat-chasing leopard enters house in Tumakuru, woman locks it
briefs.bodyText:
Tumkaru/Bengaluru: An elderly woman watching a prime-time TV show saw a more stunning drama unfold outside the screen when a leopard came rushing into the house in Kunigal taluk of Tumakuru district on Monday night.
Finding herself in the jaws of death, Narasamma jumped out of her chair, ran to the door and slammed it shut. The incident took place at Bandigaudanapalya village near Huliyurdurga. The big cat was captured in a six-hour operation.
“When the leopard walked right in, my heart stopped. I ran out as fast as I could. It’s a miracle I’m safe,” she said.
Around 9pm, the leopard, reportedly chasing a goat, stormed into the house belonging to Chikka Mariyappa. In a remarkable display of presence of mind, she trapped the leopard inside the house. The animal hid under a cot in a bedroom.
After alerted by villagers, a rescue team, including wildlife officials and tranquiliser expert Kiran from Bannerghatta, rushed to the spot.
The operation was challenging since the animal was in a confined space. After cordoning off the area, the team tranquilised the big cat and safely caged it. 
Forest officials said the leopard would be rehabilitated in deep forests.
The incident came as no surprise to villagers since they had seen the leopard prowling around for over a month, apparently in search of livestock. “We couldn’t step out after dark. We are thankful to the forest officials and rescue team for preventing a tragedy,” said Ramesh, a villager.

briefs.headline: Karnataka’s Metro fund burden increasing: Minister
briefs.bodyText:
Bengaluru: Karnataka Wednesday argued that the Union govt may facilitate negotiations and approvals, but the state has to account for every paisa spent on the project.
The state’s financial responsibility extended beyond its share of the initial project outlay, with land acquisition, implementation-related cost escalations and additional repayment liabilities arising from rupee depreciation against the dollar also falling on the state.
Bengaluru development minister Krishna Byre Gowda said the state’s share had increased across successive phases, from 79.2% in Phase I to 83.7% in Phase II and 86.9% in Phases IIA and IIB. He said the Centre’s contribution had declined even as Bengaluru’s infrastructure requirements grew. It now stands at 86:14, he added.
He flagged Metro’s accumulated operational losses of Rs 1,046 crore. Reimbursements of Rs 52 crore pending from the state govt would be released, he said.
On foreign loans routed through the Centre, Gowda said Karnataka had repaid Rs 28,958 crore, accounting for 100% of the loan amounts. BMRCL had repaid Rs 5,018 crore in loan principal so far, of which Rs 4,502 crore came from the state govt.
Red line pending for 22 months
Bengaluru development minister Krishna Byre Gowda said the 37.8km Sarjapur-Hebbal Red line proposal, submitted to the Centre in Jan 2025, remains pending for 22 months.
The state would seek PM Modi’s intervention to expedite clearance during his visit Friday. It aims to float tenders and begin work by the end of 2027.
He warned that delayed approvals were pushing up project costs. Phase I faced a 14-month approval delay, Phase II two years, Phases IIA and IIB two years and five months, and Phase III six months.
The cost escalation in Phases II, IIA and IIB stood at Rs 4,955 crore, which Karnataka is bearing entirely, according to data provided by Gowda.
Rising cost of construction is also reflected in per-km estimates, which have increased from Rs 193 crore in Phase I to Rs 352 crore in Phase II and Rs 695 crore in Phase IIIA.
On the proposed Orange line, he said its foundation stone would be laid within the next six months.
Relief for Bannerghatta Road users
Ahead of Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s visit to Bengaluru to inaugurate Namma Metro's Pink Line, civic authorities launch a cleanup drive along the corridor Wednesday
Inauguration of every stretch of Metro line brings relief to motorists and residents. It’s not because of a new transport line. Ahead of the the inauguration of Metro’s Pink line Friday, Bannerghatta Road, which was a synonym for battered roads, damaged footpaths and poor pedestrian access for months, will sport new surfaces, repaired footpaths at several locations along the elevated corridor.
The Bengaluru South city corporation has taken up facelift near Vega City Mall, Jayadeva, Tavarekere Metro station and the Dairy Circle underpass. Potholes have been filled and debris cleared from footpaths.
Some motorists dismissed the repairs as cosmetic, saying several stretches continued to have craters and lacked proper pedestrian access to Metro stations.
Paver blocks were relaid near JP Nagar 4th Phase station and in BTM 2nd Stage on Nov 5 and 6. New kerbed footpaths were developed near Dairy Circle and Spar Hypermarket on Nov 9 and 10. Roads near Tavarekere and JP Nagar 4th Phase stations were resurfaced on Nov 10, while streetlights inside the Jayadeva underpass were repaired.
3 Pink line stations renamed
Union ministry of housing and urban affairs has approved the recommendations of the state govt regarding the renaming of three stations on 
Namma Metro
’s Pink line to better reflect local identities: IIMB station is now Bilekahalli-IIMB; JP Nagar 4th Phase as NS Palya and Tavarekere as Sudduguntepalya.
Blue Line train makes progress
Namma Metro's Blue line train
Namma Metro’s Blue Line train has begun preliminary movement checks on the 6km mainline stretch between Baiyappanahalli depot and Doddanekkundi station, marking a step forward for the much-awaited ORR corridor. The exercise precedes formal trial runs, but BMRCL still has substantial station works to complete along the 19km stretch. Meanwhile, the contractor has launched the final viaduct girder between Silk Board and Baiyappanahalli during Deepavali festivities, completing all girder-launching works on the ORR corridor. BMRCL is targeting mid-2027 for its opening.

briefs.headline: AI helps Bengaluru police gather feedback from 1.5 lakh people in 3 months
briefs.deck: 112 Response
briefs.bodyText:
Bengaluru:
 Bengaluru city police completed a three-month proof of concept (POC) with a local startup to automate feedback calls to citizens who have used the 112 emergency response support system (ERSS).
Police commissioner Seemant Kumar Singh said the AI-powered initiative had helped the department collect feedback from more than 1.5 lakh people in just three months. Singh said that by using interactive voice response system (IVRS) AI technology, the average response time had been brought down to six minutes from around 15 minutes earlier. “We used to make 25,000 feedback calls per month. We introduced the AI system on a trial basis over the last three months and have collected feedback from 1.5 lakh calls,” he said.
Traditionally, feedback calls made after the closure of 112 emergency incidents were handled by trained call operators. However, the process was constrained by manpower availability, limiting the number of complainants who could be reached. The new AI-powered Voice AI-112 platform has significantly expanded the department’s outreach by enabling large-scale automated feedback collection.
Developed by VocalLabs AI, a startup, the platform uses conversational AI to conduct telephone conversations in multiple languages. 
While the AI system handles routine feedback collection, trained personnel will continue to deal with sensitive and complex interactions.
The AI-driven mechanism allows police to gather real-time citizen insights on emergency response quality, police personnel’s conduct and overall service effectiveness. The feedback will help senior officers identify areas requiring improvement and take steps to enhance public service delivery.
The department believes the initiative marks a significant milestone in leveraging AI to strengthen transparency, accountability and citizen engagement in emergency response services, while setting a new benchmark for technology-enabled, citizen-centric policing.

briefs.headline: Vietnam’s Green SM set for taxi debut in Bengaluru
briefs.bodyText:
Bengaluru
: Competition in Bengaluru’s ride-hailing market is set to intensify with Vietnam’s Green SM, the electric mobility arm of conglomerate Vingroup, preparing to launch services by Nov-end or early Dec, taking on established players like 
Ola
, 
Uber

briefs.headline: 3 arrested for late-night illegal party at Yamalur in Bengaluru
briefs.bodyText:
Bengaluru:
 A private overnight party organised without permission at a duplex house in Yamalur, with entry fees of up to Rs 2,400 and facilities for hookah, alcohol and smoking, has come under the police scanner, and three people have been arrested.
On Nov 8 around 10 pm, Central Crime Branch’s women’s protection wing received information about the late-night party on the first floor of the duplex building in Yamalur near Marathahalli, east Bengaluru.
The organisers invited young men and women through WhatsApp, Instagram and other online platforms, including HOPZYX APP and FV SOCIALS 404, without obtaining police permission. Entry fee was fixed at Rs 1,710 for men, Rs 1,080 for women and Rs 2,400 for couples, apart from additional charges.
The event involved consumption of hookah, alcohol and tobacco, smoking and playing music, besides other alleged unlawful activities. Alcohol bottles were brought to the premises, police said.
The organisers were identified as FV SOCIALS 404, represented by Parth K, Arihant Pandey, Abhinav Pandey, Anurag Chouhan and others. Chouhan is a resident of the house.
A case has been registered at Marathahalli police station under Karnataka Excise Act, Karnataka Police Act and Cigarettes and Other Tobacco Products Act (COTPA).

Bengaluru:
 Claiming to run an old-age home and needing vehicles to ferry elderly residents to hospitals and other places, a 48-year-old man rented cars from people, pledged them with others and cheated people of lakhs of rupees. Hulimavu police arrested 
Sunil Kumar
 (48), a resident of JP Nagar 8
th
 Phase and native of Kundapura in Udupi district. Cops recovered 12 cars worth around Rs 1.2 crore from him.

briefs.headline: GAIL proposes ₹123-crore waste-to-biogas plant at KCDC site in Bengaluru
briefs.bodyText:
The Gas Authority of India Limited (GAIL) has proposed setting up a 300-tonne-per-day (TPD) municipal solid waste-based compressed biogas (CBG) plant at the Karnataka Compost Development Corporation (KCDC) premises in Bengaluru. The project is estimated to cost ₹123.42 crore.
The proposed facility, spread across approximately 18 acres, will process 300 tonnes of segregated organic municipal waste daily to produce 12.6 tonnes of CBG and 21.6 tonnes of fermented organic manure (FOM) every day.
An awareness session on the project was organised on Wednesday. The biogas produced at the facility will be supplied to GAIL Gas, a wholly owned subsidiary of GAIL, for distribution as clean fuel.
According to GAIL, the plant is expected to reduce dependence on landfill disposal and provide a sustainable solution for processing the city’s organic waste. It will also have odour-control and effluent-treatment systems to minimise environmental impact.
The project is taken up as part of efforts to strengthen Karnataka’s waste-management infrastructure, aimed at promoting a circular economy by converting municipal waste into clean energy and organic manure.

briefs.headline: Bengaluru police arrest 34 in citywide drug crackdown; narcotics worth ₹12.61 crore seized
briefs.bodyText:
The Bengaluru City Police have arrested 34 people, including two foreign nationals and nine persons from other States, in a major crackdown on drug trafficking across 11 police station limits. Narcotic substances with an estimated market value of ₹12.61 crore were seized during the operation.
The seized drugs include 5.519 kg of MDMA, 46.486 kg of ganja, 72.82 grams of cocaine and 1.542 litres of hashish oil. The police also seized eight mobile phones, two two-wheelers and ₹1,000 in cash. The value of the seized narcotics were estimated to be worth ₹6.30 crore at procurement prices.
The raids were conducted in the jurisdictions of Hebbal, Koramangala, D.J. Halli, Mahalakshmi Layout, Yeshwanthpur, Adugodi, Hennur, Govindapura, Begur, Hebbagodi and Bandepalya police stations.
According to the police, the operation followed specific inputs from informants about the sale of banned narcotic substances in these areas. Cases were registered under the Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances (NDPS) Act before conducting raids at the identified locations.
During interrogation, the accused allegedly revealed that they procured drugs at lower prices from suppliers in the State, abroad and other States, and sold them at higher prices to people, including college students, for quick profits.
The police are now investigating the supply chain to identify the suppliers and uncover the wider drug distribution network. All 34 accused have been produced before the jurisdictional courts and remanded to judicial custody.

stories.headline: Why climate finance remains a recurring flashpoint at UN summits
stories.deck: As climate negotiators meet in Türkiye, the familiar battle over climate finance exposes a deeper divide. While wealthy nations count the money they mobilise, developing countries question how much actually reaches them
stories.bodyText:
As negotiators from around the world gather in Antalya in Türkiye this week and the next for the annual United Nations climate summit, a familiar argument over climate finance is once again testing the prospects for agreement. Wealthy countries point to rising sums provided for climate action. Developing countries, however, ask a harder question --- how much money is reaching them, on what terms, and how quickly enough to meet the costs of a warming world?
For India and much of the Global South, this is not an accounting dispute. It concerns protecting farms from drought, cities from floods and people from extreme heat, while expanding energy access, infrastructure and jobs through cleaner power. Climate finance can make these ambitions affordable.
Need grows faster than money available
The UN Environment Programme’s 2026 Adaptation Gap Report estimates that developing countries will need about $305 billion a year by 2035 to prepare for the increasingly severe climate impacts. Yet developed countries provided only $28.2 billion to $31.7 billion in public money for this purpose in 2024. Even if the aspiration agreed at the previous climate summit in Brazil to triple this finance by 2035 is met, it would cover only 20-29% of the estimated need.
The dispute is about the kind of finance on offer, its conditions and whether countries can access it.
Unfinished bargain
The primary issue begins with responsibility. Under the UN climate convention, developed countries accepted an obligation to provide financial resources to help developing countries address climate change. The 2015 Paris Agreement, a global treaty where nearly 200 nations agreed to cut greenhouse gas emissions and limit global warming to well below 2°C, and aim to keep it under 1.5°C, reaffirmed this.
The landmark pact says wealthy countries should lead in providing and raising climate finance. It also recognises the importance of public money and grants for countries most vulnerable to climate impacts.
For developing countries, this is not charity. It is part of the bargain behind global climate action. Countries with greater historical responsibility for global warming and more financial capacity would support those with fewer resources. This principle remains central to the UN climate process.
However, the meaning of delivery is contested. In the 2009 Copenhagen summit, wealthy nations pledged to provide and mobilise $100 billion a year for developing countries by 2020. The target was missed that year and reached for the first time only in 2022. The total rose to $136.7 billion in 2024, exceeding the target for a third consecutive year, according to the OECD, a club of rich countries.
But the headline figure does not settle the argument. The OECD total includes public finance provided directly and through multilateral development banks, export credits, and private investment attributed to public interventions. It counts the full value of loans as well as grants. In 2024, loans accounted for $68.5 billion, or 67%, of public climate finance. Grants accounted for $29.7 billion, or just a measly 29%.
A grant does not have to be repaid. A low-interest loan is cheaper than commercial borrowing, but it is still debt. For poorer countries facing high borrowing costs, the distinction matters. A loan for a revenue-earning power project is not the same as a grant for flood protection or a heat action plan.
Money announced is not necessarily money disbursed. A pledge may take years to pass approval procedures and reach the agency expected to spend it. The UN climate finance committee says there is no common accounting method for the $100 billion goal.
The OECD counts the face value of loans. Oxfam, an international non-profit, estimates the 2024 total at $32.7 billion to $44.7 billion by using a narrower measure that discounts loans and excludes some sources. These figures answer different questions, but expose the dispute over how much support represents a real transfer of resources.
Private investment is part of the answer, but cannot be the whole answer. Investors are easier to attract to projects that earn money, such as solar and wind power. It is much harder to raise commercial finance for public needs such as coastal protection, urban drainage, early warning systems or stronger health services. These may prevent enormous losses but rarely generate a direct financial return. Public funding, particularly grants, remains essential.
Larger number, unresolved questions
An agreement reached at the climate summit in Azerbaijan in 2024 was meant to move the debate forward. Developed countries agreed to take the lead in providing at least $300 billion a year for developing countries by 2035. The decision also called on all countries and institutions to work towards scaling finance from public and private sources to $1.3 trillion a year.
These are not the same commitment. The amount of $300 billion is the negotiated goal, while $1.3 trillion is a wider ambition involving many sources. The agreement did not settle how much should be grants, loans or direct government support.
India’s position reflects the concern that a larger headline number will mean little if the money is costly or difficult to access. In its formal submission, India called for at least $1 trillion a year from developed countries, primarily as grants and low-cost loans. It wants support to be affordable, predictable and accessible.
This is not a rejection of private investment or domestic fund-raising. It is an insistence that private capital cannot replace the financial responsibility for the climate crisis accepted by wealthy countries, especially where mitigation and adaptation projects offer no commercial return.
India’s needs differ from those of least developed countries and small island states, many facing acute climate risks and tight budgets. But access is a concern across the developing world. Complex applications, limited technical capacity and lengthy project preparation can keep countries from using funds that are nominally available.
The argument at the Türkiye summit is, therefore, about more than the size of the next financial target. It is about whether money is genuinely additional, whether it arrives as grants or debt, whether it can be accessed without years of delay and whether it reaches those who need it most.
Climate diplomacy cannot keep treating finance as a promise to be renewed at each summit. Developing countries are being asked to change their economies while coping with climate impacts that are already imposing heavy costs. They cannot do both on pledges alone. Until the money is predictable, affordable and accessible, the same dispute will return --- because the bargain at the heart of global climate action remains unfinished.
Soumya Sarkar is Managing Editor of IndiaClimateDialogue.net.

stories.headline: Tata Power Q2 profit jumps 32% to ₹1,652 crore
stories.deck: Thermal and hydro operations led growth, with earnings surging 158.3% to ₹1,066.66 crore in Q2.
stories.bodyText:
Tata Power reported a 32% year-on-year (YoY) increase in consolidated net profit to ₹1,652 crore for the quarter ended September, supported by a 26% rise in revenue from operations to ₹19,635 crore.
Total income rose to ₹19,964 crore from ₹16,050 crore a year ago. Earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortisation (EBITDA) increased 5.3% to ₹4,245 crore, while profit before exceptional items and tax rose 22.7% to ₹2,060.67 crore. Expenses climbed to ₹18,640 crore from ₹14,723 crore.
For the first half of FY27, consolidated net profit increased to ₹3,052.90 crore from ₹2,507.71 crore in the corresponding period last year.
Among segments, thermal and hydro operations led growth, with earnings surging 158.3% to ₹1,066.66 crore in Q2. The company attributed the improvement to the resumption of operations at its Mundra power plant, which had temporarily shut down in July 2025 due to technical issues.
Renewable energy earnings rose 7.9% to ₹1,230.14 crore, while transmission and distribution earnings declined 3.4% to ₹986.64 crore.
Separately, Tata Power announced the appointment of Sanjay Banga as chief executive officer and managing director for a five-year term beginning May 1, 2027.
Singapore court battle
Meanwhile, a Singapore court-appointed sheriff has moved to attach Tata Power’s shares in two wholly owned subsidiaries, Tata Power International Pte Ltd and Bhira Investments Pte Ltd, valued at up to S$830.77 million. The attachment notices were served on November 6.
The move follows a Singapore court order enforcing an arbitration award directing Tata Power to pay Kleros Capital Partners $490.32 million in damages, besides interest and costs.
The Singapore International Commercial Court rejected Tata Power’s challenge to the award in August 2026. The company has appealed, with the next hearing scheduled for January 19, 2027. It said it would challenge the attachment and seek to prevent any sale of the shares until the appeal is decided.

briefs.headline: Oil prices fall over 1% as hopes of Iran, Russia-Ukraine peace talks weigh on market
briefs.deck: Oil prices dropped more than 1% as hopes for progress in Russia-Ukraine and Iran negotiations emerged. Brent crude futures declined to $91.62, while US West Texas Intermediate crude fell to $85.49 a barrel. Increased production by OPEC+ and rising US crude stocks contributed to this price drop as well. Market relief followed a major prisoner exchange agreed upon by negotiators from Moscow and…
briefs.bodyText:
Oil prices fell more than 1% on Thursday as investors weighed the possibility of progress in diplomatic efforts to end the Iran war and the Russia-Ukraine conflict, easing some concerns over potential supply disruptions.
Brent crude futures declined $1.14, or 1.2%, to $91.62 a barrel by 0141 GMT, while US West Texas Intermediate (WTI) crude futures dropped $1.04, or 1.2%, to $85.49. The losses came a day after both benchmarks recovered from two-month lows, with Brent gaining 1.4% and WTI rising 0.6% on Wednesday.
Hopes of a breakthrough in the Russia-Ukraine conflict have offered some relief to oil markets. Negotiators from Moscow and Kyiv agreed to a major prisoner exchange following two days of US-mediated discussions in Abu Dhabi, which concluded on Wednesday. However, disagreements over key issues, particularly territorial control, remain unresolved. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskiy has said Kyiv hopes to make tangible progress towards ending the war this year.
The possibility of the Iran conflict avoiding further escalation ahead of next week's US-China summit has also influenced market sentiment.
"Markets are falling on expectations that behind-the-scenes efforts are underway to secure a ceasefire between Russia and Ukraine and that it is unlikely the Iran war will escalate ahead of the US-China summit next week," said Hiroyuki Kikukawa, chief strategist at Nissan Securities Investment, a unit of Nissan Securities.
He said the situation around the Strait of Hormuz could nevertheless prevent a steep decline in crude prices.
"However, given the uncertainty surrounding the Strait of Hormuz, the markets are unlikely to suffer a significant collapse," Kikukawa said.
Tensions over Iran's nuclear programme continue to complicate the prospect of negotiations. Iranian security chief Mohsen Rezaei said Tehran would not allow even a single particle of enriched nuclear material to leave the country and warned of consequences if the US launched fresh strikes. Washington has insisted that nuclear issues must feature in initial negotiations aimed at ending the eight-month-old war, although US officials have played down the need for further military action.
On the supply front, OPEC+ crude production recorded a sharp increase in October, driven largely by higher output from Saudi Arabia, even as shipments through the Strait of Hormuz continued to face disruption.
US inventory data also pointed to an increase in available supplies. Crude stocks rose by 9 million barrels in the latest week, according to figures from the American Petroleum Institute cited by market sources. The official report from the US Energy Information Administration is due on Thursday, after its release was pushed back by a day because of the Veterans Day holiday.

briefs.headline: Amid market volatility, SIP flows resilient at over 32k cr in Oct
briefs.deck: Despite recent fluctuations in the market, retail investors have remained steadfast in their commitment to mutual funds. October saw considerable net inflows into equity funds, though they dipped slightly from the previous month. The overall assets in the mutual fund sector edged up during this timeframe, showcasing investors' determination to navigate through economic uncertainties. Moreover…
briefs.bodyText:
MUMBAI: Retail investors putting money into mutual funds are increasingly showing maturity, investing in stocks that are available at lower prices, slowing down their investments in sectors that are showing a sudden spurt, while maintaining a steady pace with regards to systematic investment plans (SIPs).
In Oct, they continued to invest in large cap and mid cap schemes, but put in slightly less in small cap funds, data released by AMFI on Wednesday showed. It also showed that gross monthly SIP flows, which are almost entirely by retail investors, stood at Rs 32,160 crore, only slightly off the all-time high figure of Rs 32,490 crore in the previous month.
The first half of Oct was tough for Dalal Street, with sensex sliding to a two-year low at the sub-72K level. It was only in the last week of Oct that, boosted by foreign fund buying, the index started rallying.
AMFI data also showed that during Oct, net inflows into all equity funds together were Rs 32,994 crore, their 68th consecutive month of net inflows. This was, however, a 14% drop from Rs 38,307 crore in Sept. During the month, the industry's total assets under management (AUM) also showed a 1.2% uptick to Rs 83.4 lakh crore, from Rs 82.6 lakh crore the previous month.
According to Navneet Munot, MD & CEO, HDFC MF, "Net inflows into equity-oriented funds and SIPs continued to remain resilient in Oct, even as markets continued to witness volatility." Munot pointed out that gross redemptions from equity-oriented funds, at Rs 32,588 crore, were the lowest in recent months. "Indian investors have matured over the years and increasingly treat volatility as part of the investment journey," he said.
Within the equities segment, continued improvement in large cap inflows was an encouraging sign, in particular when valuations have become relatively attractive, suggesting investors are increasingly looking to balance their exposure across market capitalisations, said Saugata Chatterjee, president & deputy CEO, Nippon India MF.
"While inflows into small cap and mid cap funds moderated during the month, they continue to remain strong, reflecting sustained investor confidence in Bharat's long-term economic growth story."
Industry players also pointed out that in Oct, the fund industry as a whole net took in funds worth about Rs 1.7 lakh crore, compared with net outflows of Rs 1.3 lakh crore in Sept. This largely reflected the reversal of quarter-end flows in fixed income, said Hemant Kumar, chief business officer, Tata MF.
"In Oct, fixed income (funds) saw inflows of Rs 1.1 lakh crore, following the Rs 1.8 lakh crore outflow in Sept. This is largely the usual quarter-end phenomenon, with institutional liquidity returning in Oct. Overnight and liquid funds accounted for much of this reversal," Kumar said.

briefs.headline: Qualcomm India layoffs: Over 1,000 jobs at risk amid global cuts
briefs.deck: CEO Cristiano Amon has described the exercise as a performance-focused reduction, while Qualcomm’s latest annual report puts its global workforce at 57,000; the company did not respond to a request for comment on the reported India cuts
briefs.bodyText:
More than 1,000 jobs could be at risk in India as Qualcomm undertakes a global workforce reduction, although the U.S. chipmaker has not disclosed the number of positions likely to be eliminated in the country.
In an internal memo to employees on October 19, reviewed by Reuters, CEO Cristiano Amon described the exercise as a “performance-focused reduction” following the company’s annual employee reviews. Notifications to affected employees were expected to begin in November.
Mr. Amon said the move was intended to build “a stronger performance culture” and address situations where the company “has consistently fallen short of expectations”. Business priorities, organisational requirements and the skills and expertise required would determine the positions to be eliminated, he added.
Qualcomm did not respond to The Hindu’s queries on whether layoffs had commenced in India, the number of employees likely to be affected, the locations and business divisions involved, or the severance terms.
Pareekh Jain, CEO of EIIRTrend and an IT industry analyst, estimated that around 1,000 Indian employees could be affected. He said the cuts appeared to span organisational levels and were not necessarily performance-based, adding that the company was seeking to reduce global headcount and align costs with business performance.
Qualcomm’s annual report, filed with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission on November 4, put its global workforce at approximately 57,000 as of September 27, 2026. India, alongside the U.S. and China, is a key location for its sales, administrative and research and development operations.
Its 2023 Corporate Responsibility Report showed that India accounted for 36% of its global workforce of 50,257, translating into approximately 18,100 employees. The company had reported 15,404 employees in India, including temporary workers, in 2021. Its 2025 report put global headcount at 52,491 but did not provide a country-wise breakdown.
The workforce reduction comes against a weakening financial backdrop. Qualcomm reported fiscal 2026 revenue of $43.12 billion, down 3% year-on-year. Fourth-quarter revenue fell 8% to $10.32 billion, while non-GAAP net income declined 15% to $11.31 billion. The increase in GAAP net income to $13.63 billion was largely driven by a substantial tax benefit.
Meanwhile, posts on Reddit’s r/qualcomm community have described employee separations in Bengaluru and Hyderabad, including notifications on November 11. Some users claimed that employees with good performance ratings were also affected. Discussions also referred to severance packages and cuts in specialised engineering teams. These anonymous accounts could not be independently verified.
Qualcomm has not confirmed the India layoffs or the estimated number of employees affected. The company has a sizeable engineering and research footprint in India, with operations in Bengaluru, Chennai, Hyderabad and Noida, along with offices in Mumbai and the National Capital Region.
Alagunambi Welkin, president of the Union of IT and ITES Employees (UNITE), questioned whether Qualcomm had secured the necessary government approvals for the reported retrenchments. Citing the 100-worker threshold under the Industrial Disputes Act, 1947, he said prior government permission could be mandatory for retrenchments in certain establishments in Tamil Nadu.
The Industrial Relations Code, 2020, which came into force nationwide on November 21, 2025, raised the threshold for mandatory prior government approval from 100 to 300 workers in specified industrial establishments. However, Tamil Nadu has yet to notify its final State rules under the Code, having issued only draft rules in April 2022. Mr. Welkin maintained that the new Code was yet to be implemented in the State.
He urged employees facing pressure to resign to approach labour authorities before any separation proceedings are initiated.

briefs.headline: Air India’s losses narrow in H1 by ₹2,000 crore
briefs.deck: Air India is under pressure to cut costs after a consolidated net loss of ₹22,238 crore in FY2025-26
briefs.bodyText:
Singapore Airlines’ share of losses from Air India declined to S$361.7 million (approximately ₹2,720 crore) in the first half of FY2026-27, down from S$429.5 million (₹3,229 crore) in the corresponding period last year, marking a reduction of S$67.8 million (about ₹510 crore).
Based on Singapore Airlines’ 25.1% stake in Air India, the figures imply that the Tata Group-owned airline’s total losses fell to an estimated S$1.44 billion (₹10,837 crore), from S$1.71 billion (₹12,850 crore) a year earlier.
The moderation in losses offers some relief to Air India’s financial backers, even as Singapore Airlines reported a 43.9% decline in its own first-half net profit to S$134 million (approximately ₹1,008 crore), amid a sharp increase in jet fuel costs.
Air India, along with its subsidiary Air India Express, reported a consolidated net loss of ₹22,238 crore in FY2025-26, more than double the ₹10,859 crore loss recorded in the previous financial year, underscoring the financial challenges confronting the airline’s turnaround.
Singapore Airlines said in a press statement that it and Tata Sons recognise “that a transformation of this scale will take time. Both partners continue to work closely to support Air India’s journey towards profitable growth, including strengthening structural cost efficiencies, unlocking greater synergies between Air India and Air India Express, sharpening its commercial strategy to navigate current external challenges elevating its customer proposition.”
Cost rationalisation and operational efficiency have emerged as key priorities under Air India’s new Chief Executive Officer and Managing Director, Tewolde Gebremariam, who took charge on October 1.
Speaking at the Aviation India and South Asia Summit on November 3, Mr. Gebremariam said the airline was examining unit costs across every aspect of its business. It has also set up a multi-functional cost-savings team to scrutinise expenditure and identify opportunities for savings.
In an internal communication to employees in October, the CEO called for a culture of “frugality, accountability, and thoughtful decision-making.”
The airline is also looking to deepen operational synergies between Air India and Air India Express through the integration of select corporate functions, as it seeks to streamline its cost structure and improve financial performance.

briefs.headline: Sensex has rallied nearly 12%: Is it time to relook at your investment strategy?
briefs.deck: There has been a sudden turnaround in sentiment since late October and Indian equities have seen a series of upgrades in the last few days from global brokerages as well. What’s brought this about? And importantly, what should your strategy be as an investor? Which sectors will be in focus going forward? We ask experts:
briefs.bodyText:
BSE 
Sensex
 has risen by a whopping 8,600 points in the last ten trading sessions - an increase of 11.8%! That’s a remarkable feat for a stock market that has been out of favour by most standards globally this year.
Sensex and 
Nifty
 are back at their highest levels since 27 February, which was the last trading day before the US-Iran war began on 28 February.
There has been a sudden turnaround in sentiment since late October and Indian equities have seen a series of upgrades in the last few days from global brokerages as well.
What’s brought this about? And importantly, what should your strategy be as an investor? Which sectors will be in focus going forward? We ask experts:
The reasons behind the rally
The recovery in Indian equities has been driven by easing geopolitical concerns, a sharp correction in crude oil prices, a notable reversal in FII flows and decent corporate earnings reported in the second quarter. The US-midterm blow for the Trump administration has strengthened hopes of a swift end to the war with Iran.
The crude prices dropped sharply and with easing geopolitical tension the war premium in crude is likely to go down. This is particularly positive for India as it eases inflationary pressures, supports the rupee and improves the current account position.
Additionally, global investors are reassessing their exposure to expensive US technology and artificial intelligence stocks and diversifying towards emerging markets, including India.
Brent crude prices have fallen sharply
Resilient domestic economic activity and improving corporate earnings have further supported investor sentiment.
There are also hopes that the government may announce relief from long-term capital gains tax in the coming months, another positive that is drawing foreign investors’ interest.
VK Vijayakumar, Chief Investment strategist, Geojit Investments Limited lists important reasons:
1. Weakening of the AI trade after the US mid-term elections. This is positive for India which is a non-AI trade.
2. The impressive Q2 results which have come much better than expected. The near 24 % earnings growth of Nifty 50 companies is a 12-quarter high.
3. The above two factors have turned FIIs aggressive buyers in India with a buy figure of Rs 53,170 crore in November, so far. The rally is being led by largecaps which are fairly valued.
The sustainability
Some experts suggest the possibility of pullbacks of 3-5% as the market digests oil, Fed and geopolitical news. They advise staggering flow of fresh money over the next few months.
Somil Mehta, Head of Retail Research at Mirae Asset Sharekhan says that the sustainability of this rally will depend on whether corporate earnings improve and global uncertainties continue to ease. Any fresh rise in crude oil prices or geopolitical tensions could lead to volatility.
But, experts believe the medium-term outlook remains constructive, but some consolidation and intermittent volatility cannot be ruled out after the sharp recovery.
“One needs to understand that the market has seen two years and time correction and hence we would not be surprised if benchmark indices soon hit their record highs. The valuations have become more reasonable following the earlier correction backed by double digit EPS growth over next 2-3 years,” explains Sunny Agrawal, Head - Fundamental Research at SBI Securities.
What should you do?
The next big question in the minds of investors is: is it time to reassess and adjust their investment strategy? Does their portfolio require a fresh look and if yes, what are the money pockets to invest in?
According to experts, in the short term, investors should avoid chasing the rally and use market volatility to gradually accumulate quality stocks.
Sunny Agrawal says that investors holding underperforming companies with weak outlooks may use this opportunity to exit, while quality stocks should be retained.
“The focus should remain on quality-led rebalancing rather than aggressive portfolio restructuring. Investors should consider reducing exposure to expensive stocks where valuations have outpaced earnings, increasing allocation towards quality businesses with sustainable growth prospects, and diversifying excessive sector concentration,” he tells TOI.
According to him, the next phase of wealth creation is likely to be driven more by company-specific earnings growth than by a broad-based market re-rating.
“We prefer businesses delivering sustainable 15–20% earnings growth at reasonable valuations, backed by strong balance sheets and credible management execution,” he says.
SBI Securities’ expert recommends maintaining a largecap-oriented portfolio while selectively increasing exposure to quality midcaps and smallcaps.
“Long-term investors should focus on businesses benefiting from structural growth opportunities, particularly domestic capex, manufacturing, consumption, electrification and infrastructure development etc,” he says.
“Largecaps offer relatively valuation supported by earnings visibility and stability, while midcaps provide opportunities for higher earnings growth and alpha generation. Smallcaps should be approached cautiously, focusing on companies with consistent revenue growth, ROCE above 15%, manageable debt, strong cash flows and sound corporate governance,” he adds.
Tanvi Kanchan observes that on days when the Sensex rallied 2-2.5%, the smallcap index barely moved or in fact even fell!
“Large-caps offer the best combination of reasonable valuations and earnings visibility. Investors with a long term equity portfolio can look at allocation to large caps in 50%-55% which becomes the core of the portfolio,” she tells TOI.
“Midcaps offer selective opportunities where earnings growth is strong, smallcaps, one would be cautious. They have lagged this rally, valuations in many pockets are still stretched relative to earnings, and they are the most vulnerable if foreign flows reverse. A good MF allocation can include large and midcap categories to balance between two composite market caps,” she advises.
And finally, what sectors should investors focus on?
From a sector perspective, Somil Mehta, Head of Retail Research at Mirae Asset Sharekhan remains positive on banking, automobiles, healthcare, infrastructure and select consumer companies.
Tanvi Kanchan recommends financials, especially large private banks, autos, which just posted record October sales, and aviation and select consumption names where input costs fall with oil, and a contrarian position in Indian IT, which is drawing renewed interest as an alternative to global AI hardware stocks, though volatility there will stay high.
Sunny Agrawal of SBI Securities advises focus on auto, banks, capital market themes (wealth management, exchanges, stock broking, intermediaries), capital goods, specialty metals and metal products, consumption, electrical equipment, wires and cables, and industrial automation remain attractive, supported by the investment cycle in infrastructure, electrification, and digital capacity.
“Defence and aerospace manufacturing also offer long-term opportunities, although valuations warrant monitoring. Pharmaceuticals and select auto component manufacturers are other preferred areas. Investors should remain selective in chemicals, FMCG, and real estate, where earnings visibility and valuations vary across companies,” he says.
Tanvi Kanchan concludes by saying that in the long term, the case for Indian equities is intact, and arguably stronger than it was in February.
Corporate earnings are recovering, valuations are more reasonable than in 2024, and India has shown it can attract foreign capital even in a volatile world.
“Investors should keep SIPs running regardless of market levels. This is exactly when discipline pays, because the investors who stopped SIPs in March, at the bottom, missed this recovery. So yes, it is a good time to review portfolios, but not to make dramatic changes. Readjust towards quality, rebalance where allocation has drifted, keep some liquidity for corrections for averaging inflows,” she says.
(Disclaimer: Recommendations and views on the stock market, or any other asset classes or personal finance management tips given by experts and analysts are their own. These opinions do not represent the views of The Times of India.)

briefs.headline: Government bars export of lithium-ion battery waste and scrap containing black mass
briefs.deck: Black mass, the particulate powdered mixture recovered during the recycling of lithium-ion batteries, is particularly essential for India's electronics and electric vehicle as well as renewable energy storage ecosystem
briefs.bodyText:
In a positive for India’s mineral recycling industry, the Directorate General of Foreign Trade (DGFT) on Wednesday (November 11, 2026) barred the export of waste and scrap of primary cells and batteries as well as electric accumulators containing lithium-ion battery black mass.
The order would be implemented with immediate effect.
Black mass refers to the particulate powdered mixture containing lithium, nickel, manganese, cobalt and graphite that is recovered during the recycling of lithium-ion batteries.
The minerals are particularly essential for India’s electronics and electric vehicles as well as the renewable energy storage ecosystem.
In a statement, the Union Ministry of Commerce and Industry stated the move seeks to ensure that the black mass generated in India is recycled and refined within the country.
“The measure is expected to assure feedstock availability for domestic recycling and refining units, improve their capacity utilisation and encourage further investment and employment in the sector,” it stated, adding that it would also seek to address the forex outgo because of current import dependence.
The industry body the Material Recycling Association of India (MRAI) also mentioned the move would ensure that domestic recyclers and critical mineral processors may get greater access to feedstock.
Welcoming the amendment, it stated, “This is an important step towards strengthening India’s resource security, encouraging investment in indigenous recycling capabilities and building a self-reliant circular economy.”
Broadly, the measure seeks to complement the government’s existing ₹1,500 crore incentive scheme for augmenting recycling capacity for separation and production of critical minerals from secondary sources.
Industry estimates suggest about 3.2 million tonnes of e-waste, containing approximately 70,000 tonnes of end-of-life batteries, could generate an estimated 30,000 tonnes of black mass annually.
Ajay Srivastava, founder of the trade think-tank Global Trade Research Initiative (GTRI) noted that the measure would bar export of all items categorised under the nomenclature ITC (HS) 85491400.
He observed, “India recorded zero exports worldwide under this code in FY2026. The government acted to prevent future shipments and keep the material available to domestic refiners.”
Separately, he mentioned in the statement that India has more capacity to process black mass than it generates, leaving refiners short of raw material.
“Recovering more of these materials at home could reduce battery makers’ reliance on imports,” he said.

briefs.headline: Cement trader deposited Rs 14.74 lakh during demonetisation; gets tax notice but wins ITAT relief
briefs.deck: The Income Tax Assessing Officer (AO) in Balasore questioned the deposit and estimated the cement trader’s sales by comparing his business activity before and after demonetisation in 2016. Following this exercise, the assessing officer classified as much as Rs 5.72 lakh as unexplained cash and subsequently initiated proceedings against him by sending a notice.
briefs.bodyText:
A cement trader based in Balasore, Odisha, came under the 
Income Tax Department
's scrutiny after depositing Rs 14.74 lakh in cash into his bank account during the 
demonetisation
 period in November 2016.
The Income Tax Assessing Officer (AO) in Balasore questioned the deposit and estimated the trader’s cement sales by comparing his business activity before and after demonetisation. Following this exercise, the AO classified Rs 5.72 lakh as unexplained cash and initiated proceedings against him.
The trader, however, was unable to contest the department's action or file an appeal within the prescribed period because he had sustained a serious injury and was admitted to hospital. His doctor had advised him to remain on complete bed rest.
After recovering, the trader approached the Income Tax Appellate Tribunal (ITAT), Cuttack, to challenge the assessment, resulting in a delay of 736 days in filing the appeal.
The tribunal condoned the delay and agreed to examine the case on its merits.
Why did the cement trader win relief?
The trader’s advocates submitted his cash books and other supporting evidence before ITAT Cuttack.
They submitted that he had deposited Rs 14.74 lakh in cash into his bank account between November 30, 2016, and December 6, 2016. The Assessing Officer had classified Rs 5.72 lakh of this amount as “unexplained cash”. However, the cash book maintained for the cement business showed that he had Rs 14.78 lakh available in cash as of November 8, 2016, they argued.
According to the advocates, the cash book established that the trader had sufficient recorded cash on the date of demonetisation to account for the subsequent bank deposits. They therefore contended that the penalty order should be set aside.
According to an ET report, after examining the facts, ITAT Cuttack found that the man had an adequate cash balance on the date of demonetisation to make the deposits into his bank account.
The tribunal also noted that the AO had neither rejected the books of account maintained for the cement business nor disputed the net profit reported in the profit and loss account.
Explaining its decision, ITAT Cuttack said: “Once the books of accounts have been accepted, the cash available as of the date of demonitisation and SBN (specified bank note) deposits are less than the cash availability as of the date of demonitisation, we are of the view that no addition is called for in the hands of the assessee. Consequently, the addition made by the AO and confirmed by ld CIT(A) stands deleted.”
